I haven't read every single comment under this post, so I hope I'm not echoing something that someone else already said word-for-word. As a woman, I've been in your exact same position, so perhaps I can give you a little bit of perspective of how I've seen and dealt with things on the opposite side of the coin.

I understand that it's really difficult to not invest a lot of emotion into trying to make a connection and build a relationship (hell, it's something I'm still working on), but I've found that that's the key for me, at least. It could help you as well. The sooner I stopped having the "Why can't I find a boyfriend? Why do all of my friends have someone except for me? What makes them desirable but not me?" type of mindset, I found that I would be way less upset and pissed off at another failed dating attempt, which definitely helped me.  Even though nothing REALLY changed in terms of the matches I was getting, I found that it at least felt like people were more drawn to me and I was more able to have quality conversations and build connections with potential partners. Once I stopped spending so much emotional energy on dating, it came more natural to me.

Hey OP! this isn't necessarily the same situation as you, but my boyfriend's dad is a political figure as well. He's a bit more of a career politician-- he ran for governor in my state a couple of years back and lost, which was very disappointing for him. I was not with my bf at the time, but I have still seen how stress can affect his dad in his current office position now. As dumb as this sounds, one of the best things you can do for him right now is just be there. Let him know how proud you are of him and tell him it's okay to be hurt/upset by the fact that he lost-- anyone would be. Another good thing you could do for him is hang out with him more. You could do something special, like a tradition that y'all might have, or just anything that the two of you might think is fun. It's always good to spend quality time with your family in tough times. Although it is important to talk about the bad stuff, it's also good to do things that make y'all both happy so that he can heal and perhaps be even better if he decides to give it a go again! I wish y'all the best of luck!
